item_title.value: How does the Agile Manifesto address planning?

content.value: How does the Agile Manifesto address planning?
It treats a plan as something you revise rather than something you commit to once. Estimates are kept short and provisional so the scope can follow what the work actually reveals.

editor_settings.title: How does the Agile Manifesto address planning?

item_title.value: What does a typical engagement look like?

content.value: What does a typical engagement look like?
A short discovery phase to agree on the problem, then two-week cycles with something reviewable at the end of each one. You see progress continuously instead of waiting for one large reveal.

editor_settings.title: What does a typical engagement look like?

item_title.value: How do you handle changes mid-project?

content.value: How do you handle changes mid-project?
Changes are expected, so they are priced against the backlog rather than treated as exceptions. Anything new gets weighed against what is already queued, and you decide what moves.

editor_settings.title: How do you handle changes mid-project?

item_title.value: Who will I be working with day to day?

content.value: Who will I be working with day to day?
One lead stays with the project from start to finish and is your point of contact throughout. Specialists join for the stretches where their work is needed, and you always know who is doing what.

editor_settings.title: Who will I be working with day to day?

item_title.value: How do you measure whether a sprint succeeded?

content.value: How do you measure whether a sprint succeeded?
By what shipped and what was learned, not by hours logged. Each cycle closes with a short review of what worked, what did not, and what that changes about the next one.

editor_settings.title: How do you measure whether a sprint succeeded?

item_title.value: What happens after the project ships?

content.value: What happens after the project ships?
You get a handover covering the codebase, the deployment path and the decisions behind both. Ongoing support is available if you want it, but nothing is built so that you need us.
